# Ecclesiastes Chapter 6 -- Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-12

This log records all verses in Ecclesiastes Chapter 6 where the three translators significantly diverged.

---

## 6:2 — "grievous sickness" vs. "grievous affliction"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "an-evil [ra] sickness [choli]" | Literal — *choli* means sickness/disease |
| LOGOS | "a grievous sickness" | Formal equivalent |
| PNEUMA | "a grievous affliction" | Broader than "sickness" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "a grievous affliction." "Sickness" implies physical illness, which is not the point. "Affliction" preserves the suffering without misleading.

---

## 6:9 — "sight of the eyes" vs. "enjoy what you have"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-sight [mar'eh] of-the-eyes" | Literal — present reality vs. wandering desire |
| LOGOS | "the sight of the eyes" | Formal match |
| PNEUMA | "Enjoy what you have rather than desiring what you don't have" | Full interpretive expansion |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "the sight of the eyes" (EMET/LOGOS). Preserves the proverbial form. PNEUMA is accurate but loses the concision.

---

## 6:12 — "vain life" vs. "vapor-life" vs. "fleeting lives"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "his-vapor-life [chayyei hevlo]" | Creative literal compound |
| LOGOS | "his vain life" | Traditional English |
| PNEUMA | "our fleeting lives" | Dynamic, shifts to first-person plural |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "his vain life" (LOGOS). More natural in English than "vapor-life." PNEUMA's shift to first-person plural is unwarranted.

**Status:** All resolved.
